author: Jordan B Peterson
description: What does a two paragraph story about two brothers have to do with the reason your own life feels harder than it should? In this lecture Jordan Peterson takes apart the oldest story in human history, one he has been working on for forty years, and uses it to explain something far more uncomfortable than it first appears: that the world does not present itself to you as a set of neutral facts you then judge, but arranges itself in advance according to what you already value. Which means that if what you see when you look around is intolerable, there is a possible explanation you will not want to hear, and a second explanation that is worse. He traces a single line from one man’s private bitterness all the way out to war, stopping along the way to define an archaic word most people have never encountered, to explain what you are actually doing when you pay money to be frightened in a theatre, and to describe the thing that crouches at your door waiting to be invited in.
